plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets two congruent parallelograms side by side, outlined in dark blue with both diagonals drawn as thin lines, to place vector addition next to vector subtraction. In the left parallelogram the bottom edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing right and is labeled u; the slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing up and to the right and is labeled v; and the diagonal running from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner ends in an orange arrowhead and is labeled u + v. The right parallelogram repeats the same outline, but its top edge is the one labeled u with an orange arrowhead pointing right, its slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing down and to the right and is labeled -v, its bottom edge is also labeled u, and the diagonal that descends from the upper-left corner toward the lower-right corner is labeled u - v. Drawing both results inside the same shape shows that the sum and the difference are simply the two diagonals of one parallelogram. The pairing makes the point that u - v is built by reversing v and joining it head to tail with u.

interactionPlan.concept: Vector addition and subtraction are the two diagonals of the same parallelogram: u + v runs from the shared tail to the opposite corner, while u − v runs from the head of v to the head of u (equivalently, u + (−v)).
elements: parallelogram outline in dark blue (four edges)
bottom edge vector u with orange arrowhead pointing right
right slanted edge vector v with orange arrowhead pointing up-right (addition mode)
right slanted edge vector −v with orange arrowhead pointing down-right (subtraction mode)
top edge vector u with orange arrowhead pointing right (subtraction mode)
diagonal from lower-left to upper-right labeled u + v with orange arrowhead
diagonal from upper-left to lower-right labeled u − v with orange arrowhead
thin blue diagonal lines (both diagonals always drawn as construction lines)
label 'u' on bottom edge
label 'v' on right slanted edge (addition mode)
label '−v' on right slanted edge (subtraction mode)
label 'u + v' on the sum diagonal
label 'u − v' on the difference diagonal
label 'u' on top edge (subtraction mode)

interactions.label: Operation
interactions.teaches: Subtraction is addition of the opposite vector: switching to u − v reverses v into −v and the active diagonal changes from the long diagonal to the short one, making subtraction visually identical to adding a flipped vector

interactions.label: Construction step
interactions.teaches: The resultant vector is not arbitrary — it is determined by the geometric construction order: draw u, attach v (or −v) head-to-tail, complete the parallelogram, and the diagonal connecting the free tail to the free head is the result

Clicking a diagonal highlights it together with the two side vectors that compose it, making explicit which pair of edges sums to which diagonal — the sum diagonal pairs u and v, the difference diagonal pairs u and −v

demo_steps.title: Build u + v step by step
demo_steps.narration: Step through the construction: first u is drawn along the bottom, then v is placed head-to-tail at u's tip, the parallelogram is completed, and the diagonal from the origin to the far corner is revealed as u + v.

demo_steps.title: Switch to subtraction
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to u − v: the vector v flips to −v (arrowhead now points down-right), and the active diagonal switches to the one running from the upper-left to the lower-right corner — subtraction is just addition of the reversed vector.

demo_steps.title: Compare the diagonals
demo_steps.narration: Click each diagonal to see which side vectors compose it: the sum diagonal is built from u and v, the difference diagonal from u and −v. Both live inside the same parallelogram.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The sum and difference of two vectors are simply the two diagonals of the parallelogram they span — subtraction requires no new geometry, only reversing one vector before applying the same parallelogram rule.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a single parallelogram (not two side-by-side) since the toggle switches between modes. Parallelogram is wider than tall, slanting to the right (roughly 60° interior angle at lower-left). Edges in dark navy blue, ~3px stroke. Vector arrows in orange with filled triangular arrowheads. Diagonals drawn as thin (1px) blue lines always visible as construction guides; the active diagonal gets the orange arrowhead and bold label. In addition mode: bottom edge = u (arrow right), right edge = v (arrow up-right), active diagonal = lower-left to upper-right labeled 'u + v'. In subtraction mode: bottom edge = u (arrow right), right edge = −v (arrow down-right), top edge = u (arrow right), active diagonal = upper-left to lower-right labeled 'u − v'. Labels in italic serif math font. On click-highlight, thicken the selected diagonal and its two composing edges while dimming the rest. Construction steps reveal elements progressively: idle shows nothing, draw_u shows bottom edge, place_v adds the slanted edge, complete_parallelogram adds the remaining two edges, reveal_diagonal adds the active diagonal with arrowhead and label.

- Button for construction steps: the learner steps through drawing u, placing v or -v head-to-tail, completing the parallelogram, and revealing the diagonal, making the result vector depend on the order of geometric construction.

authoredContext:
Vector subtraction is similar to vector addition. To find u − v, view it as u + (−v). Adding −v is reversing direction of v and adding it to the end of u. The new vector begins at the start of u and stops at the end point of −v. See the figure for a visual that compares vector addition and vector subtraction using parallelograms.

Showing vector addition and subtraction with parallelograms. For addition, the base is u, the side is v, the diagonal connecting the start of the base to the end of the side is u+v. For subtraction, thetop is u, the side is -v, and the diagonal connecting the start of the top to the end of the side is u-v.

discrepancies: The source shows two parallelograms side by side (addition left, subtraction right); the generated figure shows one at a time behind a toggle — acceptable per multipanel rules but the default view only matches the left panel
The parallelogram proportions are slightly narrower/taller than the source, which appears wider and flatter (source ratio ~2.5–3:1 width:height vs generated ~2.2:1)
In the source, the orange edge arrows appear slightly inset from the vertices (not spanning the full edge); the generated draws them vertex-to-vertex
evaluation.notes: The parallelogram law for vector addition and subtraction is faithfully reproduced with correct topology, colors, arrow styles, and labels; the toggle-based approach for the two-panel source is acceptable and the interactions (mode switch, construction steps, diagonal highlighting) are pedagogically meaningful, though the parallelogram proportions are slightly off from the source.
action_items: Adjust vx and vy (e.g. vx=2, vy=2) to make the parallelogram wider and flatter, better matching the source proportions
Consider shortening the orange edge arrows slightly (e.g. 85% of edge length) to match the source's visual style where arrows don't quite reach the vertices
